messages:
support-jen: Hey team — escalated from customer: embeddings/rerank calls intermittently return dimension-mismatch and sometimes 401s. Also seeing 500s with high p50 latency. Customer sent request_id req_7b9c3a2e and a sample payload. Can someone triage? :eyes:

customer-poc: FYI they see this only when sending batched requests gzipped from our mobile client. Single-item calls look OK. Repro-able ~30% of the time.

alex-ml: Thanks Jen. Can you paste the exact curl they used and the error payload? Also what model + expected embedding dim?

support-jen: Model: text-embed-1024 (expected 1024 dims). Error snippet: 

```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "embedding dimension mismatch: received 768 but model expects 1024",
  "request_id": "req_7b9c3a2e",
  "batch_index": 2
}
```

Curl they used (from customer):

```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-user-..." \n  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  --data-binary @batch_payload.json.gz
```

Where batch_payload.json contains an array of string inputs. They say mobile pipeline gzips then base64 encodes transport sometimes.

ops-nick: Intermittent 401s + dim mismatch could point to two separate issues: auth token expiry/rotation and a pre-processing pipeline that corrupts payload (e.g., double-encoding). Can we get the raw gz file and the uncompressed JSON? Also confirm whether they set Content-Length vs chunked.

support-jen: Uploaded file from customer (redacted) shows gz header present. I asked them for raw gz and provided request ids for our logs: req_7b9c3a2e and req_7b9c3b1f. Logs show decode error for one batch: 

```
[2024-03-12T21:03:18Z] decode_json: invalid UTF-8 sequence at byte 512, request=req_7b9c3a2e
[2024-03-12T21:03:18Z] batch_size=4, item_lengths=[152,149,140,0], error on item_index=3
```

devon: If one item uncompresses to empty string or binary, embedding pipeline might fallback to a different model or raise mismatch. We had a case before where mobile SDK base64-encoded then gzipped, so server saw binary blob and attempted to parse as JSON array -> produced garbage embedding vector of wrong dim.

alex-ml: Repro plan: 1) ask customer to send the gz file as-is and also the result of `file -z` and `xxd -l 64` header. 2) provide a minimal curl repro for us to test both correct and double-encoded flows. 3) capture server-side trace and model shard logs for those request_ids.

support-jen: Pasted minimal repro curl that reproduces mismatch locally for me: 

```
# double-encoded pipeline (bad)
echo -n '["hello","world"]' | base64 | gzip > bad_payload.gz
curl -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" --data-binary @bad_payload.gz \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```

Response: dimension mismatch with request_id req_local_001. Works fine if I gzip the raw JSON (no base64 step).

ops-nick: Good repro. Next: we need a debug bundle for req_7b9c3a2e and req_7b9c3b1f. @sre-bot can you collect trace, worker logs, nginx access+error, and model kernel traces for those ids and upload to support bucket? Include env: prod-us-east-1 and node: gpu-14.

sre-bot: Acknowledged. Running bundle collection: collect_logs --req req_7b9c3a2e,req_7b9c3b1f --range 30m --include model-kernel --out support/1719201234_bundle.tar.gz. ETA ~ 6m.

devon: Also check whether the client sets Accept-Encoding or an extra Content-Encoding header after proxies. Some mobile proxies will recompress and add header. If server sees Content-Encoding: gzip but body already gzip+base64, decode will produce base64 string which then JSON decode produces array of characters -> wrong shape.

alex-ml: For the 401s: can we correlate timestamps with auth server logs / jwt rotation? Jen, do you have the failing req ids for 401s?

support-jen: Yes two examples: req_7b9c3c2a (401) and req_7b9c3d4f (401). They occur near the same timeframe as the dim-mismatch errors. Their mobile client uses short-lived ephemeral tokens. Customer claims their refresh path is fine. I asked for app logs.

ops-nick: I'll watch the auth service logs for token validation errors around those req ids. Also check if our gateway rejects malformed content earlier and returns 401 vs 400. Sometimes middleware order causes auth check to throw if content parsing fails.

support-jen: Customer also reported a latency spike (~p50 450ms -> 1200ms) when batch errors happen. Could be our preprocessor retrying parse or timeouts on worker. See trace snippet: 

```
[trace] req_7b9c3a2e: ingress nginx 12ms -> auth 18ms -> preprocessor 800ms (retry decode) -> model-router 340ms -> reply 40ms
```

alex-ml: That preprocessor retry is suspicious. Which version of the preprocessor are they on? If retry configured to attempt decompress+parse twice, could add >700ms. devon, any recent change?

devon: We deployed a fix last month to retry transient gzip errors once for mobile flows. If the payload is double-encoded, the first decode returns base64 text which fails JSON parse, then second attempt tries an alternate path and still fails but with more work. I'll add a guard to detect base64-like payload and short-circuit with clearer 400. I'll open a patch and we can hotfix if bundle confirms.

support-jen: Customer agreed to run the double-encode repro and send both raw gz and the header outputs. They've also provided the mobile SDK version. I'll upload all artifacts here once I have them.

alex-ml: Next actions: (1) SRE upload bundle and share link, (2) ops confirm auth log correlation for 401 ids, (3) dev to prepare guard patch and run canary, (4) support coordinate customer for final repro. Add timeline: aim to have bundle + initial root cause hypothesis in 4 hours.

ops-nick: Uploaded bundle to gs://redwood-support/1719201234_bundle.tar.gz (internal link). I grepped auth logs — both 401 reqs show token expired header at validation: `token_valid=false, reason=exp`. Looks like ephemeral tokens are indeed expiring; customer might be using cached token after sleep. Separate from gzip issue but explains two symptoms.

support-jen: Thanks all. I'll update customer: two issues: (A) double-encoded gz causing parse -> dim mismatch, repro attached + suggested client fix to ensure they gzip raw JSON not base64; (B) ephemeral token expiry causing 401s, advise refresh-on-foreground and better error handling.

customer-poc: Appreciate the quick triage. I'll push an SDK fix to ensure correct gzip behavior and add token refresh checks. Will report back with confirmation. :thumbsup:
